passage:
Coach's note, Divyansh, Under-16 swimming squad.
Pranav talked big again today. "Butterfly's for show-offs. I could do it easy, I just don't want to." He mocked Ronit's slow turns so loudly the whole lane heard. But when I asked him to try one length of butterfly, he found three reasons to go to the washroom.
I don't think this is arrogance. I think he's scared of looking bad in front of everyone. So after practice, with the pool empty, I asked if he'd try butterfly with just me: no timing, no audience. He nearly laughed it off, then nodded. He swallowed a lot of water. He came back for a second length anyway.
Plan: two quiet sessions a week. No lectures.

qa.q: How many reasons did Pranav find to go to the washroom?
qa.a: He found three reasons to go to the washroom.

qa.q: What might Pranav be afraid of underneath the loud talk?
qa.a: He may be scared of looking bad in front of everyone if he tries and fails.

qa.q: What choice did Divyansh make instead of a lecture, and why did it work?
qa.a: Divyansh offered Pranav a private try with no timing or audience, a safe chance to fail, so Pranav tried and even came back for more.

qa.q: How might Ronit feel when Pranav mocks his slow turns?
qa.a: Ronit may feel embarrassed and small in front of the whole lane.

grounding: A coach sees a teenager's boasting and mockery as cover for fear of failing in public and offers a safe, private chance to try.

passage:
Tuesday.
In drama today I told everyone the audition piece was childish and I wasn't going to waste my time on it. Sunaina laughed at my joke, her hand over her mouth, and I felt great for about five seconds. Then Ms Almeida said, "Fine, you can prompt from the wings." So I sat there watching Sunaina and the others be awful and brilliant, and I wanted to be up there so badly my stomach hurt. Truth is, if I try and I'm bad, everyone will know I'm not as good as I act. Sunaina texted after: "You'd be good. Do the reading on Friday with me? Just us two first." Just us two first. Maybe.
Dhruv

qa.q: What did Ms Almeida tell Dhruv to do?
qa.a: She told Dhruv to prompt from the wings.

qa.q: What was Dhruv afraid of beneath calling the audition childish?
qa.a: Dhruv was afraid that trying and being bad would show everyone Dhruv is not as good as the act suggests.

qa.q: What does Sunaina's offer give Dhruv, and why might it work?
qa.a: She offers a practice reading with just the two of them first, a safe chance to try without an audience.

qa.q: How might Sunaina see Dhruv's big talk in class?
qa.a: She laughed at the joke, but her text suggests she sees that Dhruv wants to take part and believes Dhruv would be good.

grounding: A teenager mocks an audition to avoid being seen failing, admits the fear in a diary and is offered a safe first try.

passage:
Monday. Everyone went for the school musical auditions today. I said musicals are for losers and sat in the back row doing impressions of Pallavi's high note till people laughed. She went red. I felt great for about a minute. Truth, since nobody reads this: I've been practising that same song in the bathroom for a month. My voice cracks on the chorus. If I went up and it cracked in front of everyone, I think I'd die. Mocking is safer. But Pallavi got called back, and I'm sitting here feeling rubbish. Ms Rao said anyone can come to the open practice on Thursday, no audience. Maybe.
Ayesha

qa.q: How long has Ayesha been practising the song?
qa.a: For a month.

qa.q: What is Ayesha afraid of under the mocking?
qa.a: Ayesha is afraid of the voice cracking in front of everyone and being exposed as failing.

qa.q: What could help Ayesha more than a lecture?
qa.a: Going to Thursday's open practice with no audience, a safe place to try and even fail.

qa.q: How might Pallavi have felt when people laughed at the impression?
qa.a: Pallavi was likely embarrassed and hurt, going red in front of everyone.

grounding: Shows a teen mocking others and refusing to try, with bravado hiding a fear of being seen to fail.

passage: At the village school in Moga, Amandeep was the loudest boy on the bench. When Eshaan missed his serve at the volleyball trial, Amandeep hooted, "My grandmother serves better!" and the others laughed. But when the PT master called his name, Amandeep stayed seated. "Volleyball is boring. I don't need trials. Everyone knows I'm the best." The master looked at him a long moment. After practice, Eshaan found him behind the water tank, flicking stones. "You were scared," Eshaan said. Amandeep started to deny it, then didn't. "What if I miss too? They'll laugh." "Like you laughed at me," Eshaan said. Then, more kindly: "Come early tomorrow. Just us. No one watching."

qa.q: Where did Eshaan find Amandeep after practice?
qa.a: Behind the water tank, flicking stones.

qa.q: What was Amandeep feeling when he stayed seated?
qa.a: He was scared of missing and being laughed at, hiding it behind boasting.

qa.q: Why is Eshaan's offer a wise idea?
qa.a: Practising early with no one watching gives Amandeep a safe chance to fail.

qa.q: How did Eshaan feel when Amandeep hooted at his serve?
qa.a: Eshaan was probably embarrassed and hurt, which is why he pointed it out later.

grounding: Shows a teen who mocks others and refuses to try to avoid being seen failing, offered a safe chance by a friend.

passage:
At the climbing wall in a Madrid sports centre, Sofia stood at the back of her PE group with her arms crossed. "This is for babies," she announced. When Lucía slipped off the second hold, Sofia laughed loudest.
Her turn came. "I'm not doing it. It's boring." Her hands, though, were shaking inside her sleeves.
The coach, Dalia, didn't argue. After class, when the hall was empty, she said, "Want to try the easy wall? No one's watching. Falling off is part of it."
Sofia hesitated, then climbed three holds and slid off onto the mat. Her face went red. She waited for Dalia to laugh.
Dalia only said, "Your left foot was good. Again?"
Sofia tried again. This time she reached the fifth hold.

qa.q: How many holds did Sofia climb the second time?
qa.a: She reached the fifth hold.

qa.q: What might Sofia have been afraid of when she called climbing boring?
qa.a: She seemed scared of failing in front of the others; her hands were shaking inside her sleeves even while she acted confident.

qa.q: Why did Dalia's offer work better than a lecture?
qa.a: She gave Sofia a private, safe chance to fail with no one watching, and answered the fall with specific praise instead of mockery.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Lucía when Sofia laughed loudest?
qa.a: Lucía probably felt embarrassed and hurt, slipping in front of everyone and being mocked for it.

grounding: Shows a teen whose boasting and mocking cover a fear of being seen failing, and how a safe chance to fail helps more than a lecture.
